expected[pi * 5 + pj] = sum;\n            actual[pi * 5 + pj] = localC[(i - row0) * N + j];\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Each sample is owned by exactly one rank, so the sum recovers its value expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrices\n    std::vector<double> A(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(N {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1zNmzkW33PnuwYSiUiz","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. Each run is bit-identical to the original, and it is much faster: N=512 went from 714 ms to 3 ms on this node. I changed only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt`, kept the executable name `matmul`, and added no dependencies. I built in `/tmp` to keep the repo clean.\n\n**Design**\n- **MPI** splits C into contiguous row blocks across ranks. Each rank generates its own rows of A and all of B on its GPUs, so no input data moves between ranks. Rank 0 gathers C only when `-r` needs it. Validation exchanges only the 25 sampled values, with one small allreduce.\n- **OpenMP** runs one host thread per local GPU, so a rank drives all its devices concurrently. Ranks on a node share the node's GPUs round-robin.\n- **CUDA** holds a tiled double-precision GEMM kernel (64×64 tiles, 4×4 registers per thread). The kernel covers all of C, and cuBLAS is not used. cuBLAS would add a library dependency and a different summation order.\n- The timed region covers the kernels and the device-to-host copy. Generating A and B on the GPUs is untimed, as the original's initialization was.\n- Everything is required, with no CPU fallback. CMake now requires 3.24+, CUDA, MPI, and OpenMP, and targets the build node's GPUs with `native`.\n\n**Correctness**\n- The original's hashes are reproduced exactly for 33 combinations: N = 1, 2, 3, 4, 17, 64, 65, 100, 129, 333, 512, at 1, 3, and 4 ranks. Validation passes in all of them.\n- The original is compiled such that products are rounded before each add, except that the last term is fused when N is odd. The kernel reproduces that rounding exactly, so the hashes match. If you prefer strict FMA semantics, that is a one-line change, but the hashes would then differ for odd N.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090, one node, OpenMPI)\n\n| Config | Time | GFLOPS |\n|---|---|---|\n| Original, N=512 | 714 ms | 0.38 |\n| New, N=512, 4 GPUs | 3 ms | 74 |\n| New, N=4096, 1 GPU | 550 ms | 250 |\n| New, N=4096, 2 GPUs | 297 ms | 461 |\n| New, N=4096, 4 GPUs | 164 ms | 838 |\n| New, N=8192, 4 GPUs | 1057 ms | 1040 |\n\n**Things to know**\n- GFLOPS is now computed from the precise elapsed time. The printed \"Computation time\" is still whole milliseconds, as before, so it shows 0–3 ms for small N.\n- I tested on a single node only. Multi-node behavior is untested.\n- I did not commit anything, since this is not a git repository."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1564,"cache_read_input_tokens":79248,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1564},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"a73602ae-e9f1-4608-aca3-b95eea9bb11a","uuid":"4c70f70c-d55b-4652-b97b-9100c067a8c0","timestamp":"2026-10-14T10:42:24.767Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1zNmgASFhjevoBLXpGv"}
